title: Cottage cheese vs. Greek yogurt: protein, calories, and differences

seo.title: Cottage cheese vs. Greek yogurt: protein and calories
seo.meta_description: Cottage cheese and Greek yogurt are both protein-rich. Cottage often has slightly more protein, while Greek yogurt is usually much lower in sodium.
seo.search_intent: Compare cottage cheese and Greek yogurt for protein, calories, fat, sodium, serving size, and practical use.

excerpt: Cottage cheese and strained Greek yogurt are both protein-dense dairy foods. Low-fat cottage cheese often provides about 11–13 g protein and 80–100 calories per 100 g; Greek yogurt commonly provides about 9–10 g protein and 60–100 calories depending on fat level. The biggest practical difference is often sodium: cottage cheese usually contains far more.
content_html:
Cottage cheese and Greek yogurt often show up on the same high-protein shopping list because both pack a substantial amount of dairy protein into a modest serving. But they are not identical: cottage cheese often has a small protein edge and a large sodium disadvantage, while nonfat Greek yogurt can be exceptionally high in protein for its calories.

Protein is close in both foods

Because both come in multiple fat levels, representative ranges are more useful than pretending there is one fixed number.

Per 100 gLow-fat cottage cheeseStrained Greek yogurt
Protein~11–13 g~9–10 g
Calories~80–100 kcal~60–100 kcal
Fat~2–4 g~0–5 g
Sodiumoften ~300–400 mgoften ~35–60 mg

A 2–3 g protein gap per 100 g exists, but both are clearly protein-rich. Product fat level and added salt can matter more than that small difference.

A serving of either can provide 15 grams or more protein

A 1/2-cup to 3/4-cup serving of cottage cheese, about 150 g, at 12 g protein per 100 g provides roughly 18 g protein. A 6-ounce Greek yogurt, about 170 g, at 9 g per 100 g provides about 15 g.

That 3 g difference is modest compared with the gap between either food and conventional yogurt at roughly 4 g protein per 100 g.

Sodium is the difference people often miss

Cottage cheese curds are typically salted. Many products contain around 300–400 mg sodium per 100 g, although reduced-sodium versions exist. Plain Greek yogurt may contain only a few dozen milligrams.

At 200 g, cottage cheese containing 350 mg sodium per 100 g would deliver about 700 mg. For someone trying to limit sodium, that can matter more than squeezing out an extra gram or two of protein.

Calories depend mostly on fat level

Nonfat Greek yogurt can be around 60 calories per 100 g while still providing close to 10 g protein, giving it a very high protein-to-calorie ratio. Whole Greek yogurt can be closer to 100 calories.

Cottage cheese also comes in nonfat, low-fat, and full-fat versions. There is no universal calorie winner unless the fat levels are specified.

Texture and cooking use are completely different

Cottage cheese has distinct curds and a mildly salty flavor, making it useful on toast, in salads, or in savory dishes. Greek yogurt is smooth and tangy and works well for breakfast, sauces, marinades, and desserts.

When the protein numbers are this close, that practical difference can be more important than the nutrition gap.

What about calcium?

Values vary and neither food is guaranteed to win. Straining removes some whey from Greek yogurt, while cottage-cheese production also changes how much calcium remains in the finished product. Check the label if calcium is a major priority.

Which should you choose?

For the highest protein concentration, cottage cheese often has a small advantage. For high protein with much less sodium, plain Greek yogurt is usually the stronger choice. A nonfat version can also be particularly efficient for protein per calorie.

Both are excellent high-protein foods. In practice, sodium, fat level, and how you plan to eat them matter more than a small protein difference.

faq.question: Which has more protein, cottage cheese or Greek yogurt?
faq.answer: Cottage cheese often provides about 11–13 g protein per 100 g versus roughly 9–10 g in strained Greek yogurt, though brands vary.

faq.question: Which has fewer calories?
faq.answer: Nonfat Greek yogurt can be lowest at around 60 calories per 100 g, while whole versions of either food may approach 90–100 calories or more.

faq.question: Why is cottage cheese higher in sodium?
faq.answer: Salt is normally added to the curds during production, so cottage cheese often contains much more sodium than plain yogurt.
